subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: What must HTTP 2xx mean when a validated Twilio SMS callback exceeds OpenClaw's dispatch quota?
rationale: Current behavior exposes rejection to Twilio and fallback handlers, while this PR intentionally redefines success to include discarded messages; tests cannot decide that delivery policy.

options.title: Preserve rejection
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 for callbacks that are not accepted, retaining Twilio error and fallback visibility until a durable overload path exists.

options.title: Add durable acceptance
options.body: Queue the validated callback durably before returning HTTP 200, then process it after capacity recovers.

options.title: Accept success-with-drop
options.body: Intentionally return HTTP 200 while discarding overflow and document that Twilio failure reporting and fallback delivery are suppressed.

recommendation.title: Preserve rejection
recommendation.body: Keep HTTP 429 for callbacks that are not accepted, retaining Twilio error and fallback visibility until a durable overload path exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged quota-separation work defines the current overload boundary that this PR changes.
